articles.title: Temporary Road Closures on Nowell Road and Pershore Road in Middleton on 26 October 2026
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has announced that roadworks on The Esplanade will commence on 4 October 2026, resulting in temporary road closures.
articles.content_html:
ONGOING STORY — Updated 28 August 2026 at 08:50. 3 source updates have been combined into this article.

Rochdale Borough Council has confirmed that roadworks on The Esplanade will begin on 4 October 2026. The works will involve a temporary closure of part of The Esplanade, starting at the junction with St Mary's Gate and extending 20 metres east along the road.

The exact timing of the roadworks will depend on weather conditions, and they are expected to take place overnight. The council will provide signage on site to inform residents and motorists of the confirmed start date prior to the works commencing.

During the closure, there will be no alternative route available for vehicles. However, a marshal will be present on site to facilitate safe access to nearby car parks for residents and visitors.

Motorists and residents should plan their journeys accordingly and remain alert for updates from Rochdale Borough Council regarding the roadworks. For further information, a map of roadworks across Greater Manchester can be viewed on the council's website.

articles.title: Pakistan Refuses to Repatriate Rochdale Grooming Gang Leader Shabir Ahmed
articles.excerpt: Pakistan has informed UK officials, including Ed Miliband, that it will not accept the return of Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, following his release from prison.
articles.content_html:
BREAKING NEWS — LIVE

Live updates, newest first.

18:42, 29 August 2026

Pakistan has declined the UK's request to extradite Shabir Ahmed, a key figure in the Rochdale grooming gang, during a meeting between UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and Pakistani officials.

15:48, 29 August 2026

During a meeting with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister Ishaq Dar stated there is no mechanism to extradite Shabir Ahmed, a key figure in the Rochdale grooming gang.

12:41, 29 August 2026

Pakistan has officially stated it will not take back Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, following discussions with UK officials, including Ed Miliband.

12:24, 29 August 2026

Pakistan has declined Ed Miliband's request to take back Shabir Ahmed, the ringleader of a Rochdale rape gang, citing a lack of legal grounds for repatriation.

12:23, 29 August 2026

Pakistan has informed UK officials, including Ed Miliband, that it will not accept the return of Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, following his release from prison.

Pakistan has officially rejected the United Kingdom's request to repatriate Shabir Ahmed, the leader of the Rochdale grooming gang, who was released from prison on July 2, 2026. The announcement came during a meeting between Ed Miliband, the UK Labour Party leader, and Mohammad Ishaq Dar, Pakistan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister.

During the discussions, Dar stated that there is no bilateral agreement between the UK and Pakistan that would allow for the transfer of individuals convicted of serious crimes, such as child sexual exploitation. He emphasised that Pakistan currently lacks the legislative framework to facilitate such repatriations, stating, "We currently do not have any legislation or formal mechanism under which we can take him back."

The UK government has been under pressure to address the situation, as it continues to fund Ahmed's probation terms, which reportedly cost thousands of pounds. The diplomatic discussions have highlighted the complexities of international law regarding the repatriation of convicted criminals, particularly in cases involving serious offences.

As it stands, the UK may need to consider alternative arrangements or negotiations if it wishes to resolve the issue of Ahmed's status. The situation remains fluid, and further diplomatic efforts may be required to address the implications of Ahmed's release and the UK's ongoing responsibilities.

articles.title: Restoration of Historic Packer Spout Steps Completed in Rochdale Town Centre
articles.excerpt: The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, a historic feature over 400 years old, has been completed, linking Rochdale Town Hall to St Chad’s Church.
articles.content_html:
The restoration of the Packer Spout steps, a unique set of historic steps over 400 years old, has been completed in the heart of Rochdale town centre. These steps, which run through the Broadfield Park Slopes, connect the major historic attractions of Rochdale Town Hall and St Chad’s Church, the oldest church in the borough, which has parts dating back to Saxon times.

Dating from before 1660, the Packer Spout steps have a rich history. They were traditionally used by mourning relatives who would ascend the steps to St Chad’s Church, scattering rue and rosemary in the churchyard as offerings for their loved ones. The steps are situated in the recently restored Broadfield Park Slopes area, which during the Victorian period was known for its notorious slum area, referred to as ‘the gank’. This area was characterised by tightly packed housing and high crime rates, with many residents working in Rochdale’s mills.

The restoration project was undertaken by Oldham contractor Maysand, which faced challenges due to the steepness of the site. A special pulley system with tracks and rollers was devised to transport the stone up the hill. The team meticulously removed all 122 steps, many of which were broken and uneven, before reconstructing both the steps and the area underneath using traditional sandstone to match the existing stone.

The completion of this restoration not only preserves a significant piece of Rochdale's history but also enhances the connection between key historical sites in the town centre. This development is likely to attract visitors interested in the town's heritage and may contribute positively to the local community and economy.

articles.title: Rochdale Competes with Exeter City for Huddersfield Town Defender Jay Sway
articles.excerpt: Rochdale is in competition with Exeter City to secure a loan deal for Huddersfield Town's young defender Jay Sway, who has recently made his League One debut.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale AFC is reportedly in a race to sign Huddersfield Town defender Jay Sway on loan, with Exeter City emerging as a rival for the 19-year-old's signature. The Spotland club had previously shown interest in Sway at the beginning of August, but faced competition from Oldham Athletic before they opted to sign Lewis Temple from Bolton Wanderers instead.

Sway has recently made his League One debut for Huddersfield in a 1-1 draw against MK Dons and also featured in the EFL Cup against Preston North End. His performances have attracted attention from several clubs, including Championship sides, leading Huddersfield to secure him on a new three-year contract following a successful loan spell at Hartlepool United.

Rochdale's need for a left-back is pressing, with only Bryant Bilongo available as a senior option in that position. Dan Moss has provided cover, playing in the recent League Two match against Crawley Town, but the club is keen to strengthen their squad further as the season progresses.

With Exeter City also interested in Sway, who has been praised for his potential, Rochdale will need to act quickly if they wish to secure his services. The outcome of this transfer pursuit could significantly impact the team's defensive options as they aim to improve their performance in the league.

articles.title: Rochdale Boroughwide Housing Appoints Paul Roberts as Permanent Chair
articles.excerpt: Paul Roberts has been appointed as the permanent chair of Rochdale Boroughwide Housing, succeeding interim chair Larry Gold. This decision aims to strengthen leadership within the organisation.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Boroughwide Housing has appointed Paul Roberts as its new permanent chair, effective immediately. He succeeds Larry Gold, who served as the interim chair during the transition period.

Roberts brings extensive experience from various leadership roles within the housing sector. His appointment is expected to enhance the strategic direction of the organisation.

The decision to appoint a permanent chair follows a review aimed at providing stability and continuity in leadership for Rochdale Boroughwide Housing.

As chair, Roberts will focus on addressing housing needs in the borough and improving services for residents. Further details on his plans are expected in the coming weeks.
